correctness.rationale: The signed digit rule can be recovered independently in F_3[[x]]: the central-binomial generating function B satisfies B^2=(1-x)^(-1), so B=(1-x)B(x^3). Its coefficients therefore have digit weights (1,-1,0). The Catalan generating function C satisfies x C=B^(-1)-1 modulo 3, with B^(-1)=(1-x)^2 B(x^3)=(1+x+x^2)B(x^3). Reading the coefficient at n+1 gives epsilon(n)=s(floor((n+1)/3)). Splitting the correlation of s by its low digit gives all three recurrences in the submission; each positive lag strictly descends, while the zero lag has normalized value one at every depth. Equivalently, alpha(v)=(-1/2)^d(v), where d counts the nonzero balanced ternary digits. For x=n+1, the classes of x mod 3 contribute (3-t) terms at lag q and t at lag q+1. Moving the x-window endpoint from 0 to 3^r flips each of the two signs for fixed h and sufficiently large r (and preserves zeros); hence the product does not change. This verifies exact stabilization on the ordinary, noncyclic blocks. For positive v, |alpha(v)|=1/2 precisely at the powers of three, with value -1/2. Two consecutive positive arguments cannot both be such powers. Finally q=0 gives R(1)=3/4 and R(2)=0, and t=0 gives R(3q)=(3/2)alpha(q), yielding exactly the proposed extremizers. The independent finite replay /tmp/opencode/frozen-digit-correlations.py used the exact integer Catalan ratio, not the digit rule, for the observed sequence; all 656 tested noncyclic correlations agreed with the balanced-ternary predictions. The proof supplies the universal argument.
residual_risks: The exact stabilization proof fixes h first and does not claim uniformity over arbitrary moving shifts or windows.
